qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Extreme switching costs in CAD (Creo) and PLM (Windchill, Arena) systems of record. Migrating decades of parametric CAD data, assemblies, and multi-tier BOM workflows incurs prohibitive operational friction and regulatory re-validation costs. Low churn (<5%), multi-year contracts with contractual annual price escalators, and 1.5x-2.5x ARR SaaS migration uplifts demonstrate durable pricing power. Tangible ROIC >100% and FY2025 GAAP ROIC of 17.4% confirm moat strength. Primary erosion threats include cloud-native CAD/PLM disruption and competitive encroachment by Dassault Systèmes and Siemens.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Indispensable CAD (Creo), PLM (Windchill/Arena), and ALM (Codebeamer) systems of record embedded in industrial and medical-device engineering workflows. Extreme switching costs generate high customer retention (<5% churn) and pricing power via contractual escalators and SaaS migration uplifts. Structurally insulated across 5 macrotrends as the digital foundation for industrial automation and AI. Fortress balance sheet with net debt under 1.2x EBITDA and 12.8x interest coverage. [5-10Y g: organic PLM/ALM/CAD volume 5.5% + price/SaaS uplift 2.5% + margin expansion 0.5% + net share repurchases 1.0%]
qualitative.evidence: FY2025 revenue reached $2,739M (+19% YoY), EBIT reached $982M (35.9% margin), and GAAP net income reached $734M. Operating ROIC (tangible) exceeds 100% and FY2025 GAAP ROIC expanded to 17.4% (5Y median 11.3%, weighed down by historical M&A intangibles from Codebeamer/ServiceMax). Free cash flow conversion is outstanding at 90.5% (FY2025 FCF $857M vs Net Income $734M; FY2026 FCF $873M). Balance sheet is conservative with $1,172M LT debt against $184M cash (net debt $988M, repayable from Owner Earnings in 1.35 years; net debt/EBITDA ~1.0x), and EBIT/interest coverage of 12.8x. Annual ARR growth of 8.5-9.25% in constant currency backed by <5% gross churn, annual price escalators (3-5%), and 1.5-2.5x ARR uplifts from on-premise to SaaS (Windchill+, Creo+) transitions. In October 2026, Schneider Electric agreed to acquire PTC for $205/share ($23.7B EV), further reflecting the indispensable strategic value of PTC's digital engineering thread.
